name: QuickJS

patches.reason: Disable Atomics without spoofing Emscripten and losing stack checks.
Select os64 allocation/date hooks and publish engine API visibility in target builds.
Add a target-private ties-even request for diagnostic %f; preserve JavaScript conversion rounding.
Fix context GC unlinking, global construction failure, lazy-global cleanup and consuming Proxy installation failure.
Retain the borrowed error during backtrace assembly when diagnostic allocation failures replace current_exception; release temporary buffer on early failure.
Return at the object/weakref teardown leak gate for an audited allocator-ledger host; raw and default destruction retain the assertions.
Add an explicitly installed browser helper for snapshots of active ordinary non-strict function arguments; needed by Dreamweaver rollovers.
Let a browser host hear each string name a global-object lookup misses, before the lookup answers as it always does; yonder's diagnostics census.

Name the method in "not a function" only for a call proved to be its fetch's: same frame, slot and value, straight-line bytecode between, and the fetched value never popped on the way, sitting under exactly the call's arguments; every other call keeps the plain message.

Refuse, with an out-of-memory exception, to make a function from a def whose bytecode emit failed: the parser never reads the buffer's sticky error, and transforming cut-short bytecode reads one instruction as another.

Throw out of memory where the parser ignored a failed allocation: a child definition with no constant-pool slot (upstream asserted), a failed closure-variable add in resolve_scope_var (used as an index, emitted as nothing, or read as a position), a failed arguments or function-name add there (captured as a wild argument slot, or looked up as a global), and a failed bytecode buffer read by get_lvalue as a SyntaxError.

Compile a module without resolving its imports (JS_EVAL_FLAG_NO_RESOLVE) and name what it imports (JS_GetModuleRequestCount/JS_GetModuleRequest), so a browser host can fetch a module graph before linking it; the pinned engine otherwise resolves through a synchronous loader at compile time. And make handled, telling the tracker, the rejected promise of a module body the engine takes as the module's error, which a host otherwise hears a second time as an unhandled rejection. And leave no module a failed resolve marked resolved, a cycle's members included, which a host whose modules outlive the failure (a page's module map) otherwise links through the NULL of the import never found or through the module the failure freed.

Give back the reference JS_SetPrototypeInternal takes on the new prototype when the object's shape copy is refused for memory; upstream returned -1 holding it, so the prototype was never freed and the runtime's teardown found it on its object list.

Apply the v flag's ClassSetCharacter rules (no unescaped ( ) [ ] { } / - |, no doubled punctuator) only to a class's atoms and a class string's; upstream applied them to every atom outside a class too, so a v-flag RegExp of `a/b` or `a-b` threw, and with it every HTML pattern holding a slash or a hyphen.

Read bytecode under a name the reader gives (JS_ReadObjectNamed): every function read takes it in place of the name written, because a browser runs one cached script under a different per-page name, which it reads back off a thrown error to know whose the error is and whether it is muted.

A module read that fails part way (an allocation refused) is unlisted and freed: upstream dropped one of its two references, leaving a half-read module on the context's list under its name, which the GC then walked through entry counts whose arrays were never allocated.
Release the source reference held by JS_ToCStringLen2 when allocating its UTF-8 export fails; upstream returned NULL holding the string, including a newly linearized rope.

configuration_scope: Atomics-disabled, stack-checked target engine and complete standalone embedding interface; slice review/merge and runner integration are tracked in JAVASCRIPT_TASKS.md
